430.t: Birthplace at Barracks and St. Claude, born 1901
430.s: Barbarin locates his birth house on Barracks and St. Claude, still standing, gives 1901 as his birth year, and says few musicians lived nearby.
430.q: Uptown Lake Corner. Okay. You're going to give us a real year you were born this time or you're going to tell us? Well, I'm going to give you 1901. All right. I'm used to that. Yeah.

183.t: Watts's birth in 1907 and the Palmyra Street neighborhood
183.s: Born in New Orleans on 17 February 1907, near Palmyra and Roman Streets; asked about music around the house.
183.q: I think it was on Palmyra Street. Palmyra near Roman. Mm-hmm.

577.t: Interview opening and birth in the French Quarter
577.s: Names, date and place are stated; Duerr says he was born in New Orleans, lived in the French Quarter until about 13 and began fooling with a banjo at about 15.
577.q: to French Quarter until I was about 13 years old and we moved out to this place here. And I didn't start to play fool around with a banjo until I was about 15, I guess.

282.t: Born at Deer Range plantation below New Orleans
282.s: Brown says he was born at Deer Range, down the river, home of Jim Robinson, a few miles from Magnolia where many musicians came from.
282.q: Oh, I born in a little country place by the name of Deerange. That was down on the other side of the river? Yeah. That's where Jim Robinson... That's where Jim Robinson from.

924.t: Birth in Versailles, Kentucky, parents and wife
924.s: Jones gives his birth date and place, his parents' names, and talks about his wife Sinobie, who attended Simmons University, and their long marriage.

290.t: Birth in St. Bernard Parish and musicians from downriver
290.s: Born July 14, 1893 in St. Bernard Parish; parents spoke French among themselves; talk of musicians from the plantations downriver such as Jimmy Newman and the Durands.
290.q: July 14th, 1893. Quatorze, yeah. Yeah. You know what that is? A St. Bernard Parish. Yeah. Do you speak French? No, no. Did your parents speak French? Yeah, they did, but they didn't speak with us, with the children, because they used that, so they wanted to say something they didn't want us to…

881.t: Born 1902 in Carrollton; moving to Palmer's Avenue
881.s: He gives his birth date, early addresses near Audubon Park and Tulane, and recalls first seeing Roy Palmer on Palmer's Avenue.
881.q: I was born in 1902, up on Hillary Street. I don't remember the number, I heard my mother say, but that's up in Carrollton.

858.t: Birth in Baton Rouge and first New Orleans bands and dance halls
858.s: Born in Baton Rouge in 1903; after moving to New Orleans he played with the Olympia band, Tuxedo band and in dance halls such as the Palace and Old Ebsen House.
858.q: But it was in Old Ebsen House Billings. And it was every night. And such musicians was Arnold McGuire, several other children. And all.

226.t: Birth in New Orleans and early memories of music
226.s: Born in 1912 in New Orleans, moved to Chicago at five; he recalls mostly the dixieland music, funeral parades and church.
226.q: My birth date? I was born April the 11th, 1912, in New Orleans, Louisiana, and moved to Chicago when I was about five years old, then spent most of my life – my early life – in the Chicago area before moving to New York, which was much later in my life.

1.s: Danny was born in the French Quarter in 1909, delivered by his midwife grandmother Victoria Barker.
1.ch: Childhood, family and the sounds of New Orleans
1.q: I was born here in New Orleans, in the French Quarter. That's on... If you have ever been to New Orleans, you will see I was smack dab... I'm a smack-dab original native of the city. I was born right in the section where the city was founded. It's called the French Quarter, the first square mile of…

73.t: Birth in Charleston and Dafts Court
73.s: Greene gives his birth date and describes the court off Rutledge Avenue where he was born and lived until 1923.
73.q: Yes. It runs right through the center of town. It's one of the main streets there in Charleston, and this is right between -- there's two streets in between, which is Race and Rutledge --
